factory-spec.purpose: Generic, portable description of a software factory: role seats in labelled terminal panes hand each other schema-checked records with status codes, a table routes every record, and the owner sees one line or one decision card.

copy-rule.item: No host names, URLs or home paths: every path is repo-relative or a config variable such as ${repo}, ${state_dir} or ${HOME}.
No keys, tokens or credentials: no page key, no key= query, no 32-hex run anywhere in the file.
No owner PII: no person's name, email, account or employer; every sample value is synthetic.
No ticket ids or record ids as requirements: a rule states behaviour, and its source file is the provenance.
Every element's text is under 240 chars and cites, in source, the repo file it was read from; a contents entry points at an id in this file with ref.
status="draft" marks a rule decided or proposed but not built in the source, or a divergence between two source files; every other rule holds on main as built.
Breadcrumbs and history in the source are left out; a rule says what holds now. Levels: MUST, SHOULD, NEVER.
Check: specs/bin/export-check.sh check runs in make lint; coverage proves every role, playbook, routes table, SOP and runbook is cited and every source exists.
copy-rule.good: A rule citing herdr/config/herdr.json and naming the key, such as break_glass.ttl_seconds (600), so a port reads the value from its own config.
copy-rule.never: A rule naming a machine, a home directory, a person, a ticket or a page link: it does not port, and the check refuses the file.

glossary.term: One agent process of one role, started by the seat script in its own labelled multiplexer tab with the role's model, effort and permission mode; named <role>-<ticket>, or a fixed name such as monitor or merger.
A worktree leased from the worktree pool with the ticket id as lease holder. The seat script leases it at seat up and returns it at seat down; a worker edits only inside its slot.

One JSON file in the event log, written only by the event script: id, UTC time, code, seat, kind, ticket, pane, a note of 240 chars or less, evidence paths, observations. The only handoff between seats.
A check that refuses a step and says why with an exit code or a record: lint before a commit, both 201s before a merge, the monitor seat before any other seat, a cap before a new seat.
The route runner loop: it reads each new record, applies the first matching routes row and writes a receipt. Its belt file is rewritten every tick; a stale belt file means the belt is stopped.
A fixed place on the line owned by one role, taking one record kind in and emitting one out: owner, interface agent, architect, worker, tester, reviewer, merger, verify, owner line.
The one line a seat receives at start: ticket id and full title, playbook path, its test pane when it has one, and the order to post a first record. Never a paragraph.
The watcher seat that comes up before every other seat, plus the labelled watcher panes in the four fixed monitoring tabs. It wakes, notifies and cleans; it never does a seat's work.

The owner's local decision page with stable, uat and dev tiers: cards of 2 to 4 options with a recommendation, plus owner messages and replies. Only the interface agent runs it; its key never enters a record.

A ticket file written only by the work-order script: problem, scope, degrees of freedom, acceptance criteria, test plan, notes, outcome. Statuses: draft, ready, in-progress, in-review, done, cancelled, stale.
The unit of work that ends in one lint, one changelog entry, one commit, one push and one checkpoint, run by the step script. A step that cannot end that way is split before it starts.
A standing default for one kind of escalation: a deadline, the records that answer it, and a default drawn from a locked decision, taken by the policy watch when nobody answers in time.
One owner-authorised command for one seat: the owner grants it on the page, the seat runs it once under bypass, and its role settings come back. Never a session or a day.
The timer-driven tick that brings back the multiplexer, bring-up, the belt, the owner page and dead seats, judging each by its process, so the line stands without a person.
The watcher that turns a stalled line, a gate record nobody took, a stale belt or a gone runner pane, into a 500 note for the monitor.
A seat's own labelled pane in its tab, where every command it runs goes through the test pane script; any other pane is refused.

section.name: small-loop
section.rule: The factory has nine roles: interface-agent, orchestrator, architect, worker, tester, reviewer, merger, monitor and player. Each role is one JSON file that validates against the role schema, and that file is the whole contract of its seat.

A role file sets runtime (default, allowed), model per runtime, effort, permission mode, read_only, owner_channel, context threshold, max_seats, label, pane layout, allow, deny, records, must, forbidden, inputs, outputs and wakes_on.

The line has nine stations in order: owner (decides on the page), interface agent, architect, worker, tester, reviewer, merger, verify (the architect checks main after a merge) and owner line (one line on the page).

Station outputs: owner request 300, interface agent request.forwarded 300, architect ticket.cut 100, worker pr.opened 100, tester test.passed 201, reviewer review.passed 201, merger merged 200, verify verified 201.
Work flows request, ticket, brief, worker, test, review, merge, verify, owner line. Every edge between two stations is a record kind and code in the routes table; no edge is a conversation.

A node is one role acting on one ticket in one labelled pane. It takes exactly the inputs its role lists, emits exactly one record plus its listed outputs, runs its playbook's numbered steps, and stops.

Architect: reads the knowledge graph, writes specs, cuts tickets with degrees of freedom, picks model and runtime per ticket, and verifies every DONE before the owner hears of it. Opus at max effort, one seat.
The architect queries the knowledge graph before cutting any ticket; a ticket that contradicts a locked decision node is not cut.
Every ticket states problem, in, out, degrees of freedom, acceptance criteria a junior seat can evidence, a generated test plan, and the model and runtime chosen for the task.
Never let two tickets that run in parallel touch one file; their write paths are disjoint.
Approval is the architect's alone: approve through the work-order script with a recorded reason only when the ticket is right to send into the system, then post ticket.cut 100.
Worker: implements exactly one ticket in one leased slot by the ticket's steps. Sonnet at high effort by default, up to 4 seats; the architect may override the model per ticket.
A worker posts work.started 100 first, then confirms the pool shows its ticket id as lease holder at its worktree path, else posts blocked 423 and stops. It never acquires or returns a slot itself.
The ticket's degrees of freedom are the only choices a worker makes; everything else in the ticket is fixed.
A worker runs lint and only the cases that prove its change, in the one labelled test pane its brief names, through the test pane script; CI runs everything else.

Close-out on the work branch: evidence per criterion, retro note, commit, push, open the PR with the criteria as body, submit and done through the work-order script, push the archive move, post pr.opened 100 with sha and pr.

Tester: runs exactly the ticket's test plan in containers in a labelled pane; posts test.passed 201 with the summary line as evidence, or test.failed 422 with the failing case, its output path and a repro command.
A tester never edits a file and never runs a test that is not in the plan; its role denies Write, Edit and every git and gh command. Haiku at medium effort, up to 4 seats.

Reviewer: read only, posts exactly one record: 422 naming path and line when a criterion lacks evidence, a file outside the ticket's paths changed, or a convention is missed; otherwise review.passed 201.
Conventions the reviewer checks: contents list, GOOD and NEVER examples, no em dash, UTC, config instead of literals. Sonnet at high effort, up to 2 seats.

Merger, one fixed seat: merges only a PR whose test.passed 201 and review.passed 201 are on the same sha, squash only; then work-order cleanup and slot release, and posts merged 200. The routes table then downs it.
A merger never resolves a conflict by hand: it posts merge.conflict 409 naming the files, and the routes table wakes the worker.
After merged 200 the architect checks the reviewer's 201 against the acceptance criteria before posting verified 201; only verified 201 reaches the owner as a done line.

Monitor: read only, haiku at low effort, one seat, up before any other seat. It wakes a waiting seat with one line naming the record id, notifies the owner of a code 400 or above meant for them, and cleans up every tick.
The monitor never does a seat's work and never closes a pane that holds an agent.

Interface agent: read only, the owner's single point of contact and the only seat with an owner channel. It turns owner messages into requests and factory records into one-line page replies with a link.

Orchestrator: read only gate between the interface agent and the factory. It validates a request, queues it with its priority and routes records by the table; it never does the work and never talks to the owner.

Player: reads one state record and emits one typed action with a one-line reason to its trace pane. Runtime is pluggable (claude, codex, system-one); it never presses keys directly or reads pixels when state exists.

No seat spawns a subagent or background process, writes prose to another agent, makes a fourth attempt, sends /compact, edits outside its allowed paths, or names a ticket to the owner without its full title.
Working roles (architect, worker, tester, reviewer, merger, player) run bypassPermissions, fenced by their deny list and playbook; interface agent, orchestrator and monitor run dontAsk and read only.
A seat reads its playbook, rendered from its role file, runs the numbered steps and stops. Every line is a command or a record; nothing else is the seat's to decide.

A ticket seat's first prompt is one line: '<ticket id> - <full title>. Playbook playbooks/<role>.md.', then its test pane and the order to run commands only there, then 'Post your first record before anything else.'
A fixed seat started with a task gets: 'You are the <role> seat named <name>. Read playbooks/<role>.md first. Your task: <task>. Post your first record before anything else.'
Every brief ends with 'Work only in <worktree>.', naming the seat's slot or checkout.
A record is one file events/YYYY/MM/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<code>-<suffix>.json, suffix five chars of a-z0-9, id equal to the file name, so N seats write at once with no lock and git never conflicts.
The writer builds each record in a .tmp file and renames it into place; no reader ever sees half a record.

Only the event script writes records. It checks code 100 to 599, seat pattern, kind enum, note length, ticket pattern and addressee role before writing; a bad field is exit 2 or 3 and nothing is written.
Only important items are events: a code at or above 300, a seat up or down, a gate result, a merge, a compaction, and the factory records the routes table needs. Routine progress is not an event.

Every seat is to write to the events dir of the checkout that brought it up, exported as COQ_EVENTS_ROOT; on main the writer still writes beside itself, so a slot's records stay in the slot until it is returned.
The check verb validates every record against the event schema and that each file name equals its id; exit 3 names each offender. Lint runs it.
The tail verb prints the newest 10 records one line each: time, code, kind, seat, ticket, note. Every seat tab and the monitoring grid loop it.
100 ACCEPTED: work taken or started: seat.up, seat.down, work.started, ticket.cut, pr.opened, notes, and a break glass in effect.
200 DONE: an integration or an owner action finished: merged, a break glass the owner granted, and policy.applied, a standing default taken.
201 PASSED: a gate passed: test.passed, review.passed, verified, and the one command of a break glass finished.
300 ROUTED: a record moved on: request.forwarded, a break glass request on its way to the owner, and the route runner's record.routed receipt.

409 CONFLICT: merge.conflict; the routes table wakes the worker with the PR, the head sha and the words merge main (fetch, merge origin/main, fix the conflicts, push, post pr.opened), then downs the merger.

422 FAILED: test.failed or review.changes, attempt 1 to 3. Attempts 1 and 2 wake the worker; attempt 3 is escalated to the architect as 423. A test.failed on a head the worker has since moved past is held.

423 BLOCKED: blocked or escalated. The first 423 on a ticket goes to the architect, the second to the owner as a decision card; a standing policy may answer one with its default once its deadline passes.
429: a seat refused over a cap, its role's max_seats or the host's max_agents. The refusal is recorded as a 429 note and nothing is built.

500: the system failed: no route, a failed route action or gate check, an unreadable or interrupted record, a failed bring-up node, a stalled line, belt or runner pane, a stalled or hand-started agent. Any 500 or more wakes the monitor.
400: the orchestrator rejects a request that fails the request schema, naming the failing key. No request schema exists in the source yet.
412 GATE_FAILED is in the locked code set, but no script or role emits it yet.
The queue is a directory of files <p0..p3>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<ticket>.json holding ticket, priority, enqueued, from (a record id) and lease. Enqueue is a write; one item per ticket; no lock.

Dequeue takes p0 before p1 and older before newer, skips leased items and, given the project, tickets the work-order next verb does not list as startable, then writes lease {holder, acquired, deadline}. Empty is exit 6.

A queue lease lasts lease_ttl_seconds from config (7200 in the source); its holder renews it; release clears it, or deletes the item with --done; sweep clears every expired lease and the monitor runs it.
The queue check verb confirms each file name agrees with its priority and ticket; a mismatch is exit 3.

Every seat layout but the player's is 1x2 plus a test pane: the agent pane '<MODEL> - <effort> - <ticket> <seat>', a 'MONITOR - <name>' event tail every 15 s, and 'test - herdr - <name>' split under it.
Any seat but the monitor is refused while the monitor seat is down, so no agent runs unwatched; only an exemption carrying an owner card id lifts this for one seat.
Scripts exit 0 ok, 2 usage, 3 validation or refused, 4 io, 6 not found, and take --json. Callers branch on the code, never on message text.

Exit 1 is a soft result: seat check differences, a stale belt, no free monitor cell, a FAILED node (bring-up, recover, belt, supervisor), a stall or a due default (flow, policy status). The work-order script adds 5, a lock timeout.
The seat script exits 3 when refused (no guard, gate, cap, name, no test pane, no slot, ticket without branch, unreachable slot, foreign process in the slot on down) and 4 on a multiplexer failure.
A step commits nothing when its checkpoint body is incomplete or lint fails; both are exit 3.
Before any multiplexer call the seat script checks the guard is on PATH for a Claude seat, then the bring-up gate, the role cap and the host cap; a refused seat leases no slot.
A worker runs commands only in its brief's test pane, through the test pane script, which refuses any pane but COQ_TEST_PANE (exit 3) and runs the command in a subshell so the pane keeps its own cwd.

Ticket statuses are closed: draft, ready, in-progress, in-review, done, cancelled, stale; an illegal transition is refused by name. evidence needs in-progress or in-review; done needs every criterion evidenced.
start refuses a test ticket whose plan is missing, has no case, has a case without intent, command or expected, or does not run in podman on a digest-pinned image.
A ticket is startable only when ready with every dependency done; an edge that would close a cycle is refused, because a loop makes next permanently empty.
Bring-up stops at the first failed node with a 500 record and a notification; every later node needs the one before it.
A seat gets at most 3 attempts on a ticket; after the third failure it posts 423 and stops. On a 423 the architect reads the evidence and splits or re-scopes the ticket, never re-prompts with prose.
The routes table takes a tester, reviewer or merger down after its gate record (field down), even when the row's own action failed, so a finished seat never holds a cap slot or its worktree.

The small loop is built in eight board steps, B0 to B7, each one ticket whose bar follows its status: B0 board, B1 worker closes its ticket, B2 route runner, B3 role seats, B4 belt on, B5 interface agent, B6 and B7 first runs.
B0: the factory board draws the lines from records and the page server serves it live.
B1: the worker role may run the work-order submit and done verbs, so a ticket reaches done on its own branch inside its own PR.
B2: a script applies the routes table to every new record and does nothing else.
B3: tester, reviewer and merger come up through the seat script when a seat row of the routes table fires, and each writes one record.
B4: bring-up starts the route runner in its reserved monitor pane and recovery and the supervisor restart it; the seat script does not yet refuse a seat while the belt is stopped.
B5: the interface agent owns the page; owner requests become records and the done line comes from a verified record. Its script is not in the source yet.
B6: a first ticket goes through the line with a seat at every station and no record written by hand.
B7: the foundation branch goes through the line: a reviewer seat passes the core specs for the first gate.
pr.opened, test.passed and review.passed carry the PR number and head sha as fields (event writer --pr, --sha), so the gate script compares heads by field, never by note.

rule.title: Station seats come up by route

section.rule: pr.opened brings the tester up, test.passed on the current head the reviewer, and review.passed on a tested head the merger, through seat rows; ticket.cut only wakes a worker, still brought up by the seat script.

The merger is seated only when the review names the head of the newest test.passed before it and of the ticket's newest pr.opened; a review on any other head is held, and the flow watch notes it as a stall.

rule.title: A moved head drops the older run

section.rule: A pr.opened on a new head while the older head has no tester result wakes the tester with that older record to drop; a tester result on any head but the newest pr.opened is held.
The merger's role asks for both 201s on the same sha, while heads_match seats it when the two heads differ only under events/; until the role says same head, the two rules can disagree.

section.name: big-loop
section.rule: The system runs the loop, never an agent: a record wakes the next seat with no human or architect prompt, a seat that posted its record is taken down by the system, and the board shows green from records only.
Every hand step seen while running the small loop becomes a routes row or a ticket, never a habit; an idle agent and a by-hand nudge are defects.

The route runner (the belt) reads each new record, matches the routes table top to bottom, asks the first matching row's when predicate if any, then acts or holds, and writes one record.routed 300 receipt to the row's role.
No runner line reads a kind, code or note except to match a row. New behaviour is a new row plus lint and a PR; only a new action verb needs runner code, and that is a design change.
The runner rereads the routes file every tick, so a new row is live on the next tick with no restart and no change to the runner.

Row: match, do, to; optional with, code, line, down, when, supersede, priority_from. match: kind, code, code_gte, attempt, attempt_lt, escalations, escalations_lt. do: enqueue, wake, seat, escalate, notify_owner, break-glass, ignore, none.
A row matches when every key it sets holds. A record without attempt counts as 1; escalations counts the escalated records the runner wrote for the ticket before this record. First match wins.

wake prompts the seat of the row's role (the role file's label with the ticket lowercased) with exactly 'record <id> playbook <dir>/<role>.md'; with pr, with merge-main and supersede add their words after the id.
notify_owner sends the same prompt to the interface agent with 'line done' or 'line decision' between the record id and the playbook path.
enqueue puts the record's ticket on the queue with the record id as from, and the record's priority when it carries p0 to p3; a record without a ticket cannot be enqueued.
escalate writes an escalated record with the row's code, the row's role as addressee and the same ticket, under the runner's own seat name.

with ticket, record or verify says what the woken seat acts on; with pr carries the record's pr and sha on the wake line, and with merge-main those plus the words merge main. Nothing else of a record is typed into a prompt.

Rows: request.forwarded 300 enqueue architect; ticket.cut 100 wake worker; pr.opened 100 seat tester, supersede; test.passed 201 when head_current seat reviewer; review.passed 201 when heads_match seat merger; merged 200 wake architect.

Rows: test.failed 422 (when head_current) and review.changes 422 below attempt 3 wake the worker, at attempt 3 escalate 423 to the architect; merge.conflict 409 wakes it with merge-main; each downs its gate seat. verified 201: line done.
Rows: blocked 423 with no earlier escalation escalates to the architect; with one, it notifies the owner, line decision; seat.down 500 and any code at or above 500 wake the monitor.
The routes schema fixes max_attempts at 3.
A record no row matches and an action that fails each become a 500 note addressed to the monitor. The runner never retries a failed action.
The runner never routes a record carrying its own seat name, which keeps a receipt from being routed again. Never write a record under the runner's seat name by hand: it is never routed.

The runner claims a record by creating state/routed/<id> exclusively before acting, then writes the outcome: done <action>, own, ignored, held <predicate>, unrouted, failed, interrupted or unreadable. It is never routed again.
At start, a ledger entry still 'claimed' means the runner died mid-action: it writes a 500 naming the record and marks it interrupted. It never repeats that wake.
To route a record again, delete its ledger file. That is the only supported way, and it is a decision, not a retry loop.
On first start the runner writes the UTC stamp to state/since and routes only records named after it, so old records wake nobody; --from-start writes a zero boundary and routes the whole log.
Every tick rewrites state/belt with UTC time and pid. Runner status exits 0 while the file is younger than stale_seconds (30 to 120) and 1 when older or missing; a stopped runner reads stale.
The runner ticks every poll_seconds (5 to 30). Ctrl-C or TERM in its pane stops it at once, and a restart over the same log routes nothing twice.
Never run two runners on one state directory: both would claim the same records. Each events directory gets its own state directory.
Records are routed in file-name order compared bytewise (C locale), so the UTC stamp orders them and code and suffix break ties.

Runner config keys: poll_seconds, runner_seat, herdr_session, events_dir, routes_file, state_dir, event_bin, queue_bin, seat_bin, roles_dir, playbooks_dir, stale_seconds; ${repo} resolves at load, and no key has a default.

The runner serves another repo via --repo, --routes and --state. That repo needs an event writer, a labelled role file per routed role, playbooks, a queue script for enqueue rows and a seat script for seat rows or downs.
Never start the runner with &, nohup or setsid; it runs in a labelled pane.
Runner state (ledger, boundary, belt) and the board output are gitignored: they are rebuilt from the log and the tree, never committed.
A second 423 on one ticket reaches the owner as a decision card of 2 to 4 options with a recommendation; the interface agent never decides for the owner.
The owner decides and talks only through the page; anything said to the owner in chat is one or two lines plus a link.
Only the interface agent runs the page tool; no other seat gets a page or an owner channel.
The interface agent waits on the page's wait loop in its own labelled pane; nothing else wakes it from the owner.
The page URL carries a key and is a credential: it never goes into a record, a checkpoint, a note or a reply.
The orchestrator validates each request against a request schema and answers a bad one with 400 naming the failing key. No request schema exists in the source yet.
Accepted work is queued with the request's priority; the architect is woken by the queue, never by the orchestrator.

The factory board is drawn only from records, tickets, roles, the routes table, the pane list and the belt state; no value is typed in. A wrong value is fixed in its record or ticket, never in the page data.
poll_seconds plus watch_seconds is at most 30, so a new record shows on the open page within 30 seconds; the config check refuses anything else with exit 3.
The watcher collects every watch_seconds and rewrites out_dir only when the entry changed apart from its time and build number; the build number lives in out_dir/.watch.json.
A pass that cannot read its inputs says so and keeps the last good page; the next pass recovers.
The page server serves index.html at /board and data.json at /board/data.json; a board never built answers 503. The open page polls data.json and redraws in place, keeping folds and scroll.
Without the multiplexer the board shows panes unavailable and trusts the seat records alone.
Each kickback lane drawn behind the line names the routes row it draws; a lane that names no row is refused.

The board's belt_state must name the file the runner rewrites each tick. In the source the runner writes factory/state/belt but the board reads factory/state/runner.json, so the live board reads the belt stopped.
The monitor wakes on every new event, so a 500 is seen without the runner waking anyone.
Decided, not built: NATS JetStream carries records between components, gRPC only the synchronous control plane, and routing stays by status code. The file queue is the offline fallback until then.
Decided, not built: a seat waits as a durable pull consumer and is woken by the publish, with no polling loop.

Every exclusive thing is a lease with a TTL (slot 14400 s, tier 86400 s, ticket 7200 s, seat 900 s) that the monitor releases on expiry with seat.stalled 500. Configured, but no script reads this file yet.

Rows: seat.up 100, seat.down 100, note 100 and record.routed 300 do ignore: no seat is woken and no receipt is written, so a runner 500 under S2-017 means a real gap or a failed action, never routine traffic.
seat runs the seat script for the row's role on the record's ticket, then the same wake line. A live seat is left as it is, so the table never asks whether a seat is up.
A row's down names a role whose seat for the ticket the runner takes down after the row's action, even when that action failed; a failure of either is one 500. A held record skips the down.
break-glass runs the seat script's break glass verb with the 200 record's id, and its exit 3 is a refusal already recorded as 423; none only writes the receipt. Neither reads a note.
The runner is serial: a seat row holds every later record until the seat script returns, about 45 s for a bring-up. Its pane must sit in a tab that holds a test pane, or every bring-up is refused.
The merger is one shared seat, so the down on merged and merge.conflict is safe only while one ticket merges at a time.
work.started 100 has no routes row, so each one still becomes a no-route 500 to the monitor; its ignore row waits on the board, which reads a row's to to place a line.
A flow watch turns a stalled line into a 500 note to the monitor: a gate record with no consumer record after stall_seconds, a stale belt, or a runner pane gone or idle at its prompt.
Which records must be picked up is the gates table of the flow config: kind, code, the role named in the note, and the consumer kinds that mean someone took it. A new gate is a row.
A gate stall is noted once for good; a belt or pane stall once per stall, its latch clearing on recovery. poll_seconds plus stall_seconds may not pass visible_within_seconds (120).
A policy watch gives an escalation a clock: when no answered_by record lands on its ticket within deadline_seconds, it writes policy.applied 200 and wakes the seat with the runner's wake line.
A policy row names the escalation (kind, code, optional attempt), a deadline, answered_by kinds, limit_per_ticket, the locked decision it draws on, and the default: wake the source seat or a role.
Never give break.glass a policy row, and never touch an escalation no row covers: it waits for the architect or the owner however old it is. The watch exits 3 on a table covering break.glass.
The blueprint page draws the system design from graph nodes and tickets: each component is done, in flight or coming up by one rule, and one with no runbook edge shows missing runbook.
Blueprint tiers dev, uat and stable: dev rebuilds its page every watch_seconds; uat and stable serve only a promoted build behind a current link. A page moves forward only by the promote script.
An owner briefing is built from tickets, records and open PRs by a script and checked against the owner standard (words per item, prose budget, full titles); a violation refuses the whole send.
An in flight figure counts tickets an open PR names plus tickets in-progress or in-review on the checkout, once per id; a ticket started on its branch stays ready on main until its PR lands.
A row's when names a gate script predicate asked before the action: exit 0 routes the record, 1 holds it, and any other exit is a 500 naming the predicate and its exit code, never a silent hold.
A held record gets one record.routed 300 receipt, 'held <kind> <code> (<id>): <reason>', and the ledger entry held <predicate>; nothing else: no wake, no seat, no down, no 500.
A hold skips the row's down on purpose: the tester seat is named per ticket and by then runs the newer head, so taking it down would end the run that counts.

Two shas are one head when they are equal, one is a prefix of the other, or their trees differ only under events/. A sha the repo lacks after one fetch from origin is an error (exit 4), never a difference.
head_current passes a record on the head of the ticket's newest pr.opened, and passes when there is none, either has no sha, or the record is that pr.opened; a record on any other head is held.

heads_match holds a review with no sha, with no test.passed before it on the ticket or one with no sha, or on another head than that test's; then it asks head_current: a merge needs a tested, current head.
A supersede row asks the gate script for the ticket's older pr.opened that has a sha, no tester result after it (test.passed, test.failed or blocked) and another head; the wake line names it.
with merge-main adds, after ' pr N sha S', ' merge main (git fetch origin, git merge origin/main, fix the conflicts, push, post pr.opened with the new sha)' to the worker's wake line.
When the gate script names an older record, a supersede row's wake line ends ' supersedes <id> (drop that run and post nothing for it)'; a malformed id or a gate failure is a 500.
The tester and worker role files do not yet mention supersedes or merge main, so the steps ride on the wake line in brackets; once the roles carry them the line can shrink to the bare tokens.

A gate record is not a stall while the consumer role's seat for the ticket reports agent_status working, until the record is busy_grace_seconds old; it is skipped without the latch, and a seat the multiplexer cannot report counts as idle.

section.name: herdr
section.rule: Every long-running thing (agent, watcher, poll, tail, server) lives in a labelled multiplexer pane. Check HERDR_ENV=1 before starting anything that outlives one command; outside it, say so and stop.
Never use &, nohup, disown, setsid or a harness background job; a background process is invisible to the owner, and invisible work reads as nothing happening.
No process or subagent runs under an agent; every long process is a labelled pane of its own.
Bring-up and recovery never start the multiplexer server: on the host a service unit owns it, in tests the harness does. A seat that started a server would hide a process under an agent.
Every multiplexer call names its session and unsets the caller's pane, tab, workspace and socket variables, so no call acts on another session or leaks a --current target into the caller's pane.
Workspaces, tabs and panes are found by label, never by a stored id, since ids change on restart. The workspace label is the repo name; a seat's tab label is the seat name.

Labels: '<MODEL> - <effort> - <ticket> <seat>' for an agent, 'MONITOR - <what>' for a watcher, 'TOOL - <what>' for a tool, 'test - <tool> <ticket>' for a suite, '<tool>-<tier>[-<ticket>]' for a tier server.
Every pane carries HERDR_PANE_ID, HERDR_TAB_ID, HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID and HERDR_SOCKET_PATH from the multiplexer; a script that finds them unset refuses to start a process.
A tab's panes come from a layout file: grid rows x columns and one slot per cell (kind agent, monitor, viewer or tool; label; command). One agent slot per seat layout, none in a monitoring layout.
Cells are built row major: the first row splits right from its left neighbour, later rows split down from the cell above, with ratios that keep columns equal.
A seat rerun repairs: a pane with the right label keeps its slot, a stray pane is relabelled into a free slot, only a missing slot is split, and a fresh non-agent pane gets its layout command.
The workspace has four fixed 3x3 monitoring tabs: 1 compaction watchers, 2 loop, events and queue, 3 shells, 4 watches. A cell is addressed N.R.C: tab, row, column.

A free cell is labelled '<N.R.C> OPEN - <what or any kind>'. take claims it, relabels it '<N.R.C> <what> - <job>' and runs the job; release stops it, waits for the prompt, returns to the neutral dir, relabels OPEN.
Never split a monitoring tab after its grid is drawn and never close a pane or tab there. A tab holding more than nine panes is reported and left alone; a busy unlabelled pane is never taken.

rule.title: No agent in a monitoring tab

section.rule: take refuses an agent command in a monitoring tab and grid reports any agent pane it finds there; agents come up only through the seat script, each in its own tab.

The same job asking again restarts in the cell it already holds, released clean first, so a re-arm never takes a second cell. With no free cell of the kind, take exits 1 and lists what holds the cells.
A pane is busy when its foreground process group is not its shell's, or a foreground process is not one of the shells the herdr config lists; release sends an interrupt only to a busy pane.

Reserved in tabs 1 and 2: 1.1.1 guard lease watcher, 1.1.2 guard watch, 1.1.3 orchestrator compaction watcher, 2.1.1 event tail, 2.1.2 queue list, 2.1.3 seat audit, 2.2.1 board watch, 2.2.2 route runner, 2.2.3 flow watch.

The page server and its wait loop each claim the first pane of the caller's tab labelled with the OPEN tool prefix and relabel it; stop restores the old labels and closes nothing; a seat with no free OPEN cell is refused, exit 3.
The seat script is the one way a seat comes up, is checked, is taken down and is audited. Door 1 is a ticket (the ticket names the seat); door 2 is a fixed seat with a task.

Launch: workspace and tab by label, panes from the layout, settings rendered from the role, seat record written, shell prompt awaited, environment line sent, agent started, seat.up 100 recorded, brief sent.

The environment rides one physical line into the agent pane only: unset inherited agent markers (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_*, CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, AI_AGENT), cd to the worktree, export the seat variables.
Seat variables: COQ_SEAT, COQ_TEST_PANE, COQ_ROLE, COQ_TICKET, COQ_ROLE_FILE, COQ_WORKTREE, COQ_REPO, RAIL_SURFACE (artifact for a Claude seat, lavish otherwise); the repo bin dir goes first on PATH.

Start with 'herdr agent start <name> --kind <runtime> --pane <agent pane> --' then, for Claude, --model --effort --permission-mode --settings <rendered file>; for Codex, -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort=...
The seat's settings file is rendered from the role's allow and deny into the seat state dir, deterministically, so check and audit compare it byte for byte with the file on disk.
Before a Claude start the seat script marks the worktree trusted in the runtime's user config, so no trust dialog blocks the start; answering the dialog with keys was rejected as a race.
The seat script waits for the shell prompt (prompt_regex within prompt_timeout_ms) before typing into a pane; no prompt in time is exit 4, and a rerun repairs.
When the agent already answers, the seat script leaves it as is and sends no second brief.
Each seat has a seat.json in its state dir: name, ticket, task, role, runtime, model, effort, worktree, lease, layout, workspace, tab, session, settings, pane, started_at, ended_at.
Seat check prints one line per difference from the seat record and exits 1 if any; a downed seat prints 'down since' and exits 3.

Seat audit reads every agent process on the host; one without a live seat record, or whose flags differ from it, is OUT OF COMPLIANCE and recorded seat.stalled 500 unless an exemption with an owner card id lifts it.
DRY_RUN=1 prints every mutating multiplexer call and writes nothing.
Caps: the role's max_seats and the host's max_agents (8 in the source). Over either, the seat is refused with a 429 record and exit 3, and nothing is built.
Briefs and wakes go in with 'herdr agent prompt <seat> "<one line>"' and land as the agent's next turn. A wake carries a record id and a playbook path, nothing else.
Commands for watcher, tool and test panes go in with 'herdr pane run <pane> "<command>"'; a worker's commands go only through the test pane script, which wraps them in ( ... ).
Keys go in with 'herdr agent send-keys <seat> <key>' or 'herdr pane send-keys <pane> <key>', named in config: interrupt C-c, escape Escape, down Down, enter Enter.
Wait with 'herdr pane wait-output <pane> --regex <re> --timeout <ms>'; read with 'herdr agent read <seat> --source visible --lines N'; liveness is 'herdr agent get <seat>'.
pane send-text and send-keys are not fenced by role rules; the test pane fence covers pane run only, so the deny list and the playbook stay the fence for the rest.

Notifications are 'herdr notification show "<code> <ticket> - <title>"'. The monitor raises one for a code of 400 or more meant for the owner; bring-up raises one on a failed node and after repairing nodes.

Retire, each step only while the agent still answers: Escape, prompt /exit, poll; answer an 'Exit and stop tasks' dialog with Down and Enter; interrupt twice; poll again. It records nothing and closes nothing.

Seat down: write a down lock, retire, close the seat's tab, return the slot it leased, set ended_at, record seat.down 100. A second down records nothing; an adopted seat is only un-named and its session keeps running.
Never close a pane that holds an agent. Only seat down closes a seat's tab, after retire; when retire does not finish, it logs that and closes the tab anyway.
Before returning a slot, down lists every process whose cwd is inside it; a process the seat did not start refuses the return (exit 3), because the return ends every process in the slot.
Commands sent to a shared pane run in a subshell, so the pane's own shell never keeps a cwd inside a slot; a slot return would kill that shell and the pane with it.

Bring-up order: multiplexer session (never started here), control plane (skipped with no health URL), guard doctor, monitoring grids, monitor seat, then every reserved pane that carries a command, judged by its process.

Recovery: halt flag, session, grids, monitor seat, belt, every seat check (a gone agent is downed), reserved panes by process, guard recover, one WARN per in-progress ticket without a live seat. It never resumes a seat silently.
A halt flag file in the state dir makes recovery change nothing; recovery never lifts it.
Releasing a stuck guard lease is a script, never a hand edit: unfreeze releases an expired guard lease, or any lease with --force (the owner's lever), and wakes the seat with one prompt.
An exemption lifts one rule (seat.audit, guard.freeze or bringup.gate) for one seat or pane until a UTC time, with the owner's card id and a reason; the schema rejects one without a card id.
Seat tests run each case against its own headless scratch session with a private HOME and config and a stub agent on PATH, then stop and delete the session on exit.
Compaction has one owner, compaction-guard: a Claude seat compacts when its turn has ended and its context is at or over the role threshold (30 percent). Codex seats are exempt.

Five hook events (SessionStart, Stop, PreCompact, PostCompact, PreToolUse) call the guard hook, SessionStart on compact also runs the resume checkpoint script, and the status line calls the guard tap; all live in the project settings.
Never start a seat without the guard's status-line tap: its sensor reads 0 percent and the seat never compacts. The seat script refuses a Claude seat when the guard is not on PATH.

At turn end over threshold the guard's Stop hook writes its checkpoint, freezes tool calls, types one /compact into the seat's own pane behind a composer check, and after PostCompact sends the resume card.
A seat's only compaction duties: answer a refused tool call (RES-400) in text and end the turn, and reply with the ack line, once, to the guard's GOV-100 memo.
After the brief, a Claude seat that acks the guard's memo and goes idle gets one continue prompt naming its ticket, full title and playbook; the seat record keeps nudged_at.
Never type or queue /compact: stacked compacts answered 'not enough messages' fire PreCompact without PostCompact, and the guard refuses every tool call until its lease runs out.

Never edit the guard, its settings or its state by hand. A governed seat is refused from releasing its own lease (tamper check), so release comes from outside: the lease watcher, a tool pane or the owner.

While a guard phase is armed or compacting every write tool is refused until the lease (freeze_seconds, default 180) runs out; the guard checks it only on a tool call, so the lease watcher releases expired ones.
The compaction trigger is a step landing, never a threshold: commit, checkpoint with the resume line in it, raise the compact request, end the turn. The threshold is the last line of defence.

Two checkpoints: the guard's own, injected at SessionStart after a compaction, and the project's CONTEXT_STATE.md stack written by the checkpoint script, newest first, appended above, never rewritten.
Decided, not built: before typing /compact the guard opens a quiet window with a 5 second countdown; watchers hold delivery, queue each wake as a file, and drain oldest first after the resume card.
Monitoring tab 1 runs 'compaction-guard watch --interval 15' and the lease watcher 'unfreeze.sh --watch 30' in its reserved cells; each logs one line on change only.
Reserved in tabs 2 to 4: 2.3.1 break glass restore watch, 2.3.2 policy watch, 3.3.1 to 3.3.3 blueprint dev, uat and stable servers, 4.1.1 turn watch, 4.1.2 record watch, 4.1.3 supervisor log.
A reserved pane is healthy when its label is its owner's and a process other than the shell is in its foreground; a label alone proves nothing. health prints ok or FAILED per reserved pane.
Never type into a reserved slot labelled open under a job someone else runs: it is reported left alone with one 500, and the panes after it are still repaired.

One belt node serves recovery and the supervisor: the runner pane runs and the belt is fresh, else the runner restarts in its slot through monitors take and the node waits settle_seconds for a fresh belt.

A supervisor tick runs at boot and every 30 s after the last ends: halt flag, multiplexer answers, podman answers, bring-up, belt, owner page and its wait loop, then the seats. A timer runs it, never a seat.
Every supervisor step is killed after step_timeout_seconds (120) and every command after its own timeouts key, so a hung command costs one tick, never a stuck supervisor.
The supervisor never forks the multiplexer server: when the session does not answer it starts the host's service unit. A podman that does not answer gets podman system migrate.

A seat is dead when its pane is gone or no claude or codex runs in its foreground. Seen dead on two ticks grace_seconds apart, it is started again by the seat script in the same pane, keeping its lease.
Re-seat skips a seat younger than up_seconds, one under a fresh down lock, an adopted seat and the monitor; a closed ticket's seat is downed; a third death in window_seconds is a 500 for a person.
When the owner page server is not alive, the supervisor serves it again joined to its session, then its wait loop, in the tab that holds the page's panes; a page stopped on purpose is left alone.
The supervisor's units are rendered from templates and installed from the main checkout only; from a worktree slot install refuses with exit 3, since a slot is deleted when its ticket closes.

A turn watch prompts the architect once per seat whose turn ends, judged from seat records and the pane footer, never from a busy flag that reads idle during a long command; it finds the architect by name.
A record watch prompts the architect once per new gate record in the checkout or any slot, announcing each file name once across roots and nothing older than its own start.
Adopt makes a running Claude session a role's seat in place: seat record, agent name, pane label and settings for its next start, seat.up 100. It types nothing, so the session keeps its context.
Adopt is refused (exit 3) for a pane with no claude agent, a session id the multiplexer contradicts, a name another agent holds, or a second pane for a role that has its seat.
A seat restarts from a transcript with --resume on door 1 or 2: the runtime starts that session under the role's flags, from the checkout the session ran in; a runtime other than claude is refused.
A seat whose layout has a test slot gets its own test pane in its own tab, exported as COQ_TEST_PANE and named in the brief, so seats test in parallel and never queue on one pane.
Never move a test pane's shell into the leased slot: it stands in the checkout that brought the seat up, because a slot return ends every process inside the slot.
Break glass flips one seat to bypass for one owner-authorised command: the seat script reads the owner's Grant on the page itself, never trusting a record, and refuses 423 when any check fails.
An owner answer authorises one action once: its state file is created no-clobber and never deleted, so a second use is refused 423. The action is one plain command, with no ; & | backtick $( or *.
While it lasts, a pre and post tool hook lets exactly that command through once and blocks, with exit 2, any other command holding the head of a lifted rule and the same command a second time.
The role's settings come back when the command's 201 lands or after break_glass.ttl_seconds (600, at most 3599); a sweep pane restores every 15 s, and a seat that keeps bypass is a 500 in the audit.
Every break glass flips the seat to bypassPermissions, a dontAsk seat included; the guard hook fences the lifted territory and the ttl bounds the rest.
The halt flag stops the supervisor as it stops recovery: a tick that finds it prints HALTED and changes nothing until the flag is removed.

After a compaction a SessionStart hook (matcher compact) prints the seat's own newest CONTEXT_STATE.md checkpoint into its context, so it resumes from its own resume line; it always exits 0, a miss is one line.
A seat's rendered settings carry the same compact hook, bounded by resume_checkpoint.hook_timeout_seconds (10); the shells key lists the shell names a busy pane is judged against.

section.name: a2a
section.rule: A record is the only thing one seat hands another: ticket id, status code, evidence paths, observations. A seat never writes prose to another agent; the only prose in the system goes to the owner.
Required: schema_version '1.0.0', id, at, code, seat, kind. Optional: ticket (or null), pane, to, note, evidence, observations, attempt, sha, pr, action, answer, policy. No other field is allowed.
id: <YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<3 digit code>-<5 of a-z0-9>. at: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ in UTC. code: integer 100 to 599. seat: ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$. ticket: ^WO-[0-9]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}$ or null.
Kinds are a closed enum. System kinds: seat.up, seat.down, seat.stalled, gate, test, review, merge, deploy, compaction, blocked, escalation, note, record.routed, break.glass, policy.applied.

Factory kinds: request.forwarded, request.accepted, request.rejected, ticket.cut, work.started, pr.opened, test.passed, test.failed, review.passed, review.changes, merged, merge.conflict, verified, rejected, escalated.
to names the addressee role of a routed or escalated record: interface-agent, orchestrator, architect, worker, tester, reviewer, merger, player or monitor. It is a field, never note text.
evidence: up to 20 paths. observations: up to 5 of {path, line, saw, expected}, saw and expected at most 240 chars each, written as --observe 'path:line:saw:expected'.
attempt is 1 to 3; a record without attempt counts as attempt 1.

The factory record requires role, ticket and attempt and adds sha, pr and repro (one command, 240 chars); it has no pane or to. Its kinds are the factory kinds plus blocked, seat.up, seat.down, compaction and note.
The log's records follow the event schema; the factory shape is the target. The writer emits sha and pr but not role or repro, so a role travels in the seat name and a repro in the note or evidence.
note is at most 240 characters and the writer refuses a longer one (exit 3). It is for the owner's line and the monitor's screen; nothing branches on it.
Never route on a note or any prose: the runner matches kind, code, attempt and escalations only. An if on a kind, code or note inside the runner is behaviour nobody can read from the table.
A failure record (422, 423) carries one repro command and at least one observation. Proposed: the writer refuses one without them (exit 3); not enforced yet, and the writer has no repro flag.

Kickback is a script call, never a message: the event writer with kind test.failed, code 422, attempt N, --observe 'path:line:saw:expected' and --evidence path; the table wakes the worker with the record id.
A seat cannot be prompted with free text: its brief is one line naming ticket, title and playbook, and every later prompt is a record id plus a playbook path.
Specs, tickets, test plans and playbooks live in files; a prompt or record carries only their id or path, never their content. The seat reads the record, never a sentence.
A woken seat reads the record named in its wake and posts exactly one record for it.
Prose limits: record note, observation saw and expected, and repro, 240 chars each; a role must line 240; a role forbidden line 160. Anything longer goes in a file and the record carries its path.
Owner-facing text is one or two lines plus a link, and every ticket in it carries its id and full title, never a bare id or a pointer such as 'the blocked one'.
A node that lacks something posts blocked 423 with observations; it never asks the next seat.
A seat is replaceable by another runtime (Claude, Codex, System One) because only the record crosses the boundary.
Every routed record but an ignored one gets one record.routed 300 receipt naming kind, code, record id, action, addressee and any down, or held and why, with the routed record's path as evidence.

Every record a node, seat, gate or monitor emits carries one code. Factory records use the HTTP-shaped set; guard records use families GOV, CMP, RES, RCV, OPS: 1xx-2xx normal, 3xx controller, 4xx pushback, 5xx recovery.

Some kinds the role files list (spec.proposed, owner.answer, owner.message, recovered, owner.notified, routed, turn, death, stuck) are outside the writer's enum, which refuses them; seats post them as note.
sha (7 to 40 hex) and pr (an integer from 1) name the PR head a record is about; the runner refuses a malformed one with a 500 and types nothing into the seat.
action is the one command a break glass asks for, exactly as the seat will run it; answer is the id of the 300 request, which is also the id of the owner's card on the page.
policy names the policies row (POL-id) a policy.applied record applies; its answer is the id of the escalated record the default answers, and the default text rides in the note.
A break glass is records of kind break.glass on the seat it is for: 300 request, 200 granted, 423 refused, 100 in effect, 201 command finished, 204 role settings restored and verified.

section.name: determinism
section.rule: The script writes the ticket, never the model: every field, transition, note, evidence line and archive move goes through the work-order script.
Progress is appended with the note verb and each criterion is evidenced with --observed through the evidence verb; nothing in a ticket file is edited by hand.
Never hand-edit the generated work-order index or epic READMEs; the script regenerates them, and a reindex check fails on a ticket file at the top level.
A ticket with no parent owns a directory named for it; a child is written into its parent's directory; a closed ticket moves to archive/<year>/. Files never move on a status change.
Approval is a script verb; approving without the review surface needs an explicit flag and a reason, and both are recorded in the ticket.
The change log is one dated entry file per change with frontmatter; CHANGELOG.md is rendered from the entries, never edited, and check fails when it differs from a fresh render.
Every scripted entry is a new file, never an overwrite: <tree>/YYYY/MM/YYYYMMDD-<name>.<ext>, UTC dates, frontmatter with title, at and type; a same-day, same-name entry gets a suffix.
Each tree has one script that owns its format and takes --json; never hand-write an entry. A fix for an earlier entry is a new entry carrying resolves: <suffix>, never an edit.

A change someone must reason about later carries a BREADCRUMB comment at the fix site: what broke (file and line), why it mattered, why this fix and the rejected alternative, its cost, and the record id.
A format with no comment syntax carries its breadcrumbs in a field, such as the role file's breadcrumbs array, or in the nearest file that has comments, which names the change.
Each playbook is rendered from its role file by a pure render (same input, same output); lint re-renders and fails on drift, so a hand edit to a playbook fails the build.
Lint validates every config/*.json against the schema beside it, every role against the role schema, every layout against the layout schema and every record against the event schema.
Every tunable (model, effort, port, path, label, threshold, retry count, timeout, URL) lives in a schema-validated config. No script carries a default: a missing key is exit 3 naming the key.

Config strings may carry ${repo}, ${HOME}, ${project}, ${tier}, ${ticket} and ${ENV:NAME}, resolved at load. No absolute path or hostname sits in a config file, so it lifts to object storage unchanged.
make lint runs every static check in one container built from a digest-pinned base, with the repo mounted read-only and no network; CI runs the same script in the same image on every push to main.

Lint: specs valid, under 1000 lines, no em dash, pointers resolve; graph check and spec sync; configs, layouts, roles; playbooks in sync; changelog rendered; records valid; shellcheck; no merge markers; contents; exports.

A step lands through one script: checkpoint body check, lint (a failure commits nothing), changelog entry, stage, commit, push, then the checkpoint commit and push. It queues no compaction unless asked.
Every directory with executable code has a Makefile; a target is a thin call into a script, so the same thing runs from a pane, CI and a container; make help lists the targets.
Every Containerfile base is pinned by digest, never by a bare tag; the lint image names its human tag in a comment and is built for amd64 and arm64, so CI agents of either kind can run it.

Every schema sets additionalProperties false, so an unknown key fails validation. Record and config schemas pin schema_version with a const (1.0.0); the page tool's takes a semver, and layouts and graph nodes carry none.

Closed enums: kinds, roles, route actions (enqueue, wake, seat, escalate, notify_owner, break-glass, ignore, none), with (ticket, pr, record, verify, merge-main), when (head_current, heads_match), line, down, runtimes, effort, modes.
Pin the multiplexer and guard releases the scripts were proven against (the source parses herdr 0.9.0 JSON shapes and runs compaction-guard 1.2.8); a new release is proven by the suites first.

Suites run in Podman with no network, the multiplexer stubbed or a scratch session. Locally run only the cases that prove the change; CI runs lint on every push to main and the blueprint suite when its inputs change.
The architect writes the test plan into the ticket before work starts and the tester runs exactly it. Test templates are schema-based and reused before a new one is written.
Anything written more than once is a template rendered by a script: briefs, playbooks, tickets, test plans, harnesses, SITREP pages, the change log and records.
Specs are XML under 1000 lines, valid against the spec schema, and point at graph nodes and other specs by id instead of restating them; a dangling pointer fails lint.
The knowledge graph is one JSON node per file, written only by the graph script. A locked node is never edited; a change is a new node with a supersedes edge; every edge target must exist.
A decision node needs an owner source; an agent proposes with status proposed and waits for the owner.
The first 100 lines of every file an agent opens route: a contents list, the binding rules, then pointers to the rest. A file that cannot route in 100 lines is split.
Every AGENTS.md, README, runbook, SOP, playbook and spec opens with a contents list, and every rule carries GOOD and NEVER examples.
UTC everywhere an agent writes: logs, file names, tickets, ledgers, checkpoints, graph nodes, specs. YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ in attributes and file names, ISO 8601 with seconds in JSON records.
Never use the em dash character in specs or markdown; lint fails on it.
Never write PII, credentials, tokens or internal hostnames anywhere in the repo; sample data is synthetic and obviously fake.

A run is reproduced from its files: the event log (one file per record, UTC id), the runner ledger, queue items, ticket files with notes and evidence, change log entries and checkpoints. Chat is never a source.

Routing is a pure function of log and table: run the runner once with --from-start and a fresh --state over a copy of the log, with the multiplexer stubbed as its suite does, to re-derive every route.
A board entry is re-derived from the same files with collect --root DIR --now UTC --number N --panes FILE (a saved pane list) and validated against its schema before anything is written.
A bring-up is reproduced from its role file and layout: DRY_RUN=1 prints every multiplexer call, and the rendered settings are deterministic, so check and audit compare them byte for byte.
Every task is cut into steps that each end in a commit and a checkpoint; carrying several finished steps in context is a defect.
Monitoring, compaction and failover are scripts in panes; a human is notified, never required. A step that depends on someone remembering it is a script that does not exist yet.
Graph check fails when a Component node has no defined_in edge to a Runbook node, except a closed grandfathered list in the graph config, so a new component ships with its runbook.
Route action ignore marks the ledger entry ignored and writes nothing else, no receipt and no 500. An ignore row has no to, which the schema enforces, so nothing reads a station from it.
A spec export leaves the repo, so lint checks it: it parses, every element's text is under 240 chars and cites a source, and it holds no home path, host, key, email, ticket id or record id.

The routes schema is kept twice, beside the table and in the factory schema dir; on main the two are identical, and the factory lint validates the table against the one beside it, so a change lands in both.
The flow and policy watches read every tunable from schema-checked configs and branch on no kind, code or note outside a table row, as the runner does; a new stall or default is a row.

section.name: port-notes
section.rule: Every verb is a bash 4+ script under set -euo pipefail. PS 5.1: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' and Set-StrictMode -Version Latest; native commands never throw, so check $LASTEXITCODE after each one.
The exit codes 0, 2, 3, 4 and 6 are the contract. PS 5.1: end with exit N and run scripts with powershell -File, since -Command can collapse a failing exit to 1; callers read $LASTEXITCODE.
jq builds and reads every JSON file. PS 5.1: ConvertFrom-Json and ConvertTo-Json; always pass -Depth to ConvertTo-Json (the default of 2 flattens nested objects); 5.1 has no -AsHashtable.
python3 jsonschema validates every config and record. PS 5.1 has no Test-Json (it arrived in 6.1): keep python3 jsonschema in the lint container, or load a .NET JSON schema library.
Records are UTF-8 JSON with no BOM. PS 5.1 Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 adds a BOM that python json rejects; write with [IO.File]::WriteAllText(p, s, (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding $false)).
Writes go to <file>.tmp, then mv into place. PS 5.1 runs on .NET Framework, where [IO.File]::Move throws if the target exists: Move for a new file, [IO.File]::Replace to overwrite, same volume only.
The ledger claim uses set -C so exactly one writer creates the file. PS 5.1: [IO.File]::Open(p, [IO.FileMode]::CreateNew) throws when the file exists, the same atomic claim; close the handle at once.
Times come from date -u, +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ and +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ. PS 5.1: [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'", [Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture).
Lease deadlines use GNU date -d '+N seconds' and compare ISO strings. PS 5.1: [DateTime]::UtcNow.AddSeconds(N); compare [DateTime] values, or ISO strings with an ordinal comparison.
Records are ordered by file name under LC_ALL=C, bytewise. PS 5.1 Sort-Object is culture-aware and case-insensitive; sort with [Array]::Sort(names, [StringComparer]::Ordinal).
The 5-char id suffix comes from /dev/urandom through tr -dc a-z0-9. PS 5.1: draw from [Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator]::Create() over a-z and 0-9 so concurrent writers cannot collide.
Belt age is stat -c %Y against date +%s. PS 5.1: ([DateTime]::UtcNow - (Get-Item p).LastWriteTimeUtc).TotalSeconds.

Nothing uses inotify: the runner, the board watcher and the tail panes poll every 5 to 30 s. PS 5.1: a Start-Sleep loop is the match; FileSystemWatcher can drop events under load, so keep the poll as the truth.
The runner waits with read -t, not sleep, because bash defers a TERM trap until sleep ends. PS 5.1: Start-Sleep in short slices inside try/finally; Ctrl-C stops the loop and finally still runs.
Cleanup on failure is trap ... EXIT, such as returning a slot lease taken before a refusal. PS 5.1: try { } finally { } around the whole verb.
Config paths are ${repo}/a/b with forward slashes and no absolute path. PS 5.1: keep '/' in config and build real paths at the edge with Join-Path from the repo root.
Scripts find their tree with readlink -f on BASH_SOURCE. PS 5.1: $PSScriptRoot and $PSCommandPath, then Resolve-Path for the repo root.
Scratch work goes to mktemp -d directories, removed when done. PS 5.1: New-Item -ItemType Directory (Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ([Guid]::NewGuid())), removed in finally.

Frontmatter, labels and cell positions are cut with awk and sed -E. PS 5.1: -match, -replace and Select-String use .NET regex; re-test each pattern, since POSIX classes such as [[:space:]] do not exist there.
Ticket frontmatter is found with the line pattern ^---$, which misses a '---' line ending in CR. PS 5.1 writes CRLF by default: write ticket and record files with LF, or strip CR before matching.

The env line for a pane is quoted with printf %q. PS 5.1: single-quote each value and double any embedded single quote; build the line for the pane's own shell (export for bash or zsh, $env:NAME= for PowerShell).
Each multiplexer call drops the pane, tab, workspace and socket variables with env -u. PS 5.1: save them, Remove-Item Env:NAME, make the call, restore them in finally.
Inherited agent markers are unset by a sed over env. PS 5.1: Get-ChildItem Env: | Where-Object Name -match '^(CLAUDECODE|CLAUDE_CODE_.*|CLAUDE_PID|CLAUDE_EFFORT|AI_AGENT)$' | Remove-Item.
The audit reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline for every agent process. PS 5.1: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process, match the agent binary in CommandLine, then compare its flags with the seat record.

Lint and suites run in rootless Podman: --network=none, --userns=keep-id, a :ro,Z repo mount. PS 5.1: Podman on Windows runs in a podman machine; keep no network and the read-only mount, and prove keep-id and :Z there first.
shellcheck -S warning lints every .sh in the lint step. PS 5.1: Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer from PSScriptAnalyzer over every .ps1 at warning and error severity, inside the lint step so a finding fails it.
GNU make is the entry point of every directory. Windows has none by default: install it, or keep one dispatcher script whose verbs mirror the targets one for one, each a thin call into a script.

Pane shells are zsh or bash and the seat script waits for prompt_regex '[$%>❯] *$'. PS 5.1: the prompt ends 'PS ...> ', which the '>' covers; confirm the regex against the real prompt and keep it in config.

Every multiplexer call goes through one wrapper that names the session and unsets the pane variables. PS 5.1: keep one wrapper function; if the multiplexer runs only inside WSL, call it through wsl.exe in that one place.

Slots come from treehouse, a pool of git worktrees leased with the ticket id as holder. PS 5.1: without treehouse, one pool script owns git worktree add and remove plus a lease file per slot; nothing else calls it.
The worktree pool lives outside the repository: an in-repo pool is bound into every container, taken as build context and staged by git add -A. The same holds on Windows.
Scratch sessions keep socket paths short: a Unix socket name holds at most 108 bytes and a long scratch HOME broke it. PS 5.1: keep scratch roots short.
On the source host a systemd unit owns the multiplexer server and no seat starts it. PS 5.1: a scheduled task or a service owns it, never an agent's shell.

Only a leading ~ is expanded, to $HOME, and seat state lives in a state dir under the user's home. PS 5.1: $HOME or $env:USERPROFILE, with the state root read from config, for example under $env:LOCALAPPDATA.
Seat names lowercase the ticket with ${var,,}. PS 5.1: .ToLowerInvariant(), never the culture-sensitive ToLower().
Lookups use find | sort, grep -rl and xargs -r. PS 5.1: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File -Filter *.json, Select-String -List and ForEach-Object; guard empty input explicitly.

Before a Claude start the seat script sets hasTrustDialogAccepted for the worktree path in the runtime's user config. PS 5.1: key it by the path as the runtime reports its cwd; write the JSON with -Depth and no BOM.
Hooks and the status line call the guard by path from the project settings. PS 5.1: install the guard where the agent runtime runs and render that path per host from config; never commit a user path.
Page builders use python3 and not jq, because jq is missing from Git Bash on Windows; keep python3 the only dependency of a page builder.
The supervisor is a systemd user timer (20 s after boot, 30 s after each run) with lingering on. PS 5.1: a Task Scheduler task at logon repeating every 30 s, running the same script once per trigger.
Each supervisor step runs under timeout with a kill-after. PS 5.1: Start-Job, Wait-Job -Timeout N, then Stop-Job and Remove-Job; never wait on a native command without a bound.
The briefing builder and checker need node 20 or newer and a PR listing command; offline, pass a saved PR listing file. PS 5.1: install node; the scripts are plain ES modules.

section.name: workflows
section.rule: The routes table is the workflow: each route below is one row in table order, one edge from a record kind and code to one action; first match wins, and a record no row matches is a 500 to the monitor.
max_attempts is 3: a gate failure at attempt 3 is escalated, never woken to the worker again.
kind, code and attempt compare to the record (no attempt counts as 1); code_gte is a floor; escalations counts the escalated records the runner wrote for the ticket before this one.
Each diagram below is a standalone mermaid flowchart of a few rows; join their edge lines under one 'flowchart LR' header to draw the whole line. Node ids are the same in every diagram.

A row's when names the gate predicate asked before its action, head_current or heads_match, and supersede true asks for an older head to drop. Putting an existing predicate on another row needs no runner change.
Predicate exit 0 routes the record; 1 holds it with one held receipt and the ledger entry held <predicate>, skipping the action and the down; any other exit is a 500, never a silent hold.
The gate script reads the event log and git and writes nothing. Verbs: same-head A B, when <predicate> --id ID, supersedes --id ID. Exit 0 ok, 1 hold or differ, 2 usage, 4 io or an unresolvable sha.

rule.title: A held merge is a stall

section.rule: A held review.passed has no consumer record, so the flow watch notes it as a stall after stall_seconds: that is the alarm a held merge raises.
busy_grace_seconds (1800): a gate record whose consumer role's seat for the ticket reports working is not a stall, and is judged again next tick, until the record is that old.
section.action: Prompt the seat of the row's role (its label, ticket lowercased): 'record ID playbook DIR/ROLE.md'; after the id, with pr adds ' pr N sha S', with merge-main those and ' merge main (...)', supersede ' supersedes ID (...)'.
Run the seat script for the row's role on the record's ticket, then send the wake line; a seat already up is left as it is.
The wake line to the interface agent with 'line done' or 'line decision' between the record id and the playbook path.
Put the record's ticket on the queue with the record id as from, and the record's priority p0 to p3 when it carries one.
Write an escalated record with the row's code, addressed to the row's role, on the same ticket, under the runner's seat name.
Mark the ledger entry ignored and nothing else: no receipt, no 500, no multiplexer call.
Run the seat script's break glass verb for the record's seat with the record id; its exit 3 is a refusal it already recorded as 423.
Nothing but the record.routed receipt: the record was seen.
section.route: An owner request the interface agent forwarded waits in the queue for the architect.
A cut ticket wakes its worker. This row only prompts: the worker seat is still brought up through the seat script.
The worker opened a PR. The tester seat for the ticket is brought up if it is not, and woken with the PR and head sha, and with the older head it replaces when one is still being tested.
The tester passed the PR on the current head. The reviewer is brought up and woken with the PR and head sha, then the tester is taken down. A pass on a head the worker moved past is held.
The tester failed the PR on the current head. The worker is woken with the record, then the tester is taken down. A failure on a head the worker moved past is held.
The third failure on the current head is not woken to the worker again: it is an escalated 423 to the architect, and the tester is taken down.

The reviewer passed the PR on the head a test passed, or one that differs only under events/. The merger is brought up and woken with the head sha, then the reviewer is taken down. Any other head is held.
The reviewer asked for changes. The worker is woken with the record, then the reviewer is taken down.
The third change request is an escalated 423 to the architect, and the reviewer is taken down.
The merger merged. The architect is woken to verify main, then the merger is taken down.
The merge conflicted. The worker is woken with the PR, the head sha and the words merge main, then the merger is taken down.
The architect verified the merge. The interface agent gets the done line for the owner.
A seat is blocked. The first 423 for a ticket is escalated to the architect.
A second blocked 423 for the ticket: the interface agent gets a decision line for the owner.
Housekeeping: the seat script recorded a seat coming up. Ledger entry only.
Housekeeping: a seat went down, the record a down field produces. Ledger entry only.
Housekeeping: a seat noted something. Notes are never routed on.
Housekeeping: a receipt another seat name wrote; the runner already skips its own.
A break glass request: the interface agent puts a Grant or Refuse card on the page for the owner.
The owner granted it: the runner runs the seat script's break glass verb with this record, which re-checks the page itself.
A break glass was refused; the monitor is woken with the record.
A break glass is in effect: seen and receipted, nobody woken.
The one command finished: seen and receipted, nobody woken.
The policy watch took a standing default: seen and receipted, so it is not a no-route 500.
The role settings are back and verified: seen and receipted, nobody woken.
A seat went down badly. The monitor is woken with the record.
Any other code of 500 or more. The monitor is woken with the record.
section.gate: A pr.opened 100 with no test.passed, test.failed, blocked on its ticket within stall_seconds (90) is a stall naming the tester.
A test.passed 201 with no review.passed, review.changes, blocked on its ticket within stall_seconds (90) is a stall naming the reviewer.
A test.failed 422 with no pr.opened, blocked, escalated on its ticket within stall_seconds (90) is a stall naming the worker.
A review.passed 201 with no merged, merge.conflict, blocked on its ticket within stall_seconds (90) is a stall naming the merger.
A review.changes 422 with no pr.opened, blocked, escalated on its ticket within stall_seconds (90) is a stall naming the worker.
A merge.conflict 409 with no pr.opened, blocked, escalated on its ticket within stall_seconds (90) is a stall naming the worker.
A merged 200 with no verified, rejected, blocked on its ticket within stall_seconds (90) is a stall naming the architect.
