procedure.title: Run the route runner
procedure.step: Run 'route.sh run' in its labelled monitors pane (bring-up plugs it into its reserved slot), never with &, nohup or setsid. It ticks every poll_seconds (5 to 30).
One tick and exit: 'route.sh once'. Belt: 'route.sh status' exits 0 while the belt file is fresher than stale_seconds, else 1. Suite: 'make -C factory test', in Podman, multiplexer stubbed.
The first start routes only records written after it; pass --from-start on that first start to route the log already there.
Keep the runner pane in a tab that holds a test pane: seat and down rows call the seat script, which finds that pane from its tab, or every bring-up becomes a 500.
Stop it with Ctrl-C or TERM in its pane; it stops at once, and a restart over the same log routes nothing twice.

procedure.title: Run the runner against another repo
procedure.step: Pass --repo DIR, --routes FILE and --state DIR: --routes replaces routes_file, --state replaces state_dir, and everything else hangs off ${repo} in the runner config.
The other repo needs an events dir written by an event writer, a role file with a label for every routed role, and a playbook for every role a wake reaches.
It also needs a queue script when the table has an enqueue row, and the seat script when it has a seat row or a down field.
Give each events directory its own state directory: it holds the ledger, the first-start boundary and the belt file.

procedure.title: Add routing behaviour
procedure.step: Add a row to the routes table, which its schema validates; run make lint; open a PR.
The runner rereads the table every tick, so the row is live on the next one with no runner change and no restart.
A new do or a new row field is the only thing that needs runner code, and that is a design change to the routes contract, not a row.
To route one record again on purpose, delete its ledger file under the state dir's routed/; that is the only supported way.

procedure.title: Runner symptoms and fixes
procedure.step: 'no route for KIND CODE': no row matches. Add a row, or the record is not one the factory routes.
'route failed ... agent prompt': the target seat is not up and the row is a wake. Bring it up with the seat script; the record is not retried.
'seat.sh --ticket T --role R failed': the seat script refused (monitor down, a cap, no test pane, ticket not started). Fix that, then route the record again on purpose.
'seat.sh --down NAME failed': a foreign process holds the slot, or the seat never existed. The row's own action was still done.
'routing of record ID was interrupted': the runner died between claim and finish, so the wake may or may not have gone. Look, then re-send by hand.
'unreadable record': a file in the log is not JSON. Fix or remove it; the runner ignores it from then on.
A record never routed: it predates the first start without --from-start, or it carries the runner's own seat name.

procedure.title: Run and tune the flow watch
procedure.step: Bring-up starts the runner in 2.2.2 and the flow watch in 2.2.3 of the monitors grid; never start them from a shell of your own.
'bringup.sh --check' lists the runner and flow panes; 'recover.sh --check' lists the belt; 'recover.sh --apply' restarts the runner pane and waits for a fresh belt.
'make -C factory flow-status' lists the stalls present now, exits 1 when one is and writes nothing; 'make -C factory flow-once' runs one tick and writes any new note.
Tune the flow config: poll_seconds plus stall_seconds may not pass visible_within_seconds (120), or the watch exits 3 at start. A new gate is one gates row; the script is not touched.
A stall 'KIND CODE ID has no ROLE record': check the belt, then the role's seat; it is not noted again. To note a gate record again on purpose, delete its latch file.

procedure.title: Add and run a standing policy
procedure.step: Find the escalation in the routes table: an escalate row, or a notify_owner row with line decision.
Find the locked decision that answers it in the graph. If there is none, the escalation has no policy: the owner decides.
Add a policies row with that kind and code, a deadline, the answered_by kinds, a limit per ticket and the decision's id.
Run the factory lint and suite; a case checks that every row matches an escalating routes row and cites a node that exists. The script is not touched.
The watch lives in slot 2.3.2. 'make -C factory policy-status' lists waiting escalations and exits 1 when one is past due; 'make -C factory policy-once' applies what is due.
No default for a blocked seat means: no row covers it, it predates the first start, an answered_by record landed, or the limit was reached.

procedure.title: Break glass rules
procedure.step: Only the owner authorises, on the page: an answer whose id is the request's record id, choice Grant, card naming the seat and the exact command. A 200 record is a notice, never the authority.
One action per authorisation, never a session or a day: the answer is spent once through a no-clobber state file that is never deleted.
The action is one plain command with no newline, ;, &, |, backtick, $( or *; a multi-step fix is a script, and the script's path is the action.
For that one command the seat runs with bypass permissions, and a second command is still denied.
The role settings come back when the command's follow-up record lands or after the ttl (600 s, at most 3599), whichever is first.
A seat that keeps bypass after that is a seat.stalled 500 from the seat audit.
Every one is a record, and the board shows each as a row.

procedure.title: Break glass, end to end
procedure.step: The seat or the architect writes the 300 request with --action; the routes table sends it to the interface agent as a decision line.
The interface agent puts a Grant or Refuse card on the page with Refuse preselected, so Grant is never the default.
The owner answers; Grant becomes a 200 record, anything else a 423.
The runner sees the 200 and runs the seat script's break glass verb, which takes seat and command from the 300 request and refuses 423 unless every check holds.
The seat's settings are rewritten: bypass, covering deny rules removed, the command allowed, a pre and post Bash hook added; the role's copy is kept, 100 is written and the seat prompted.
The hook lets that command through once and blocks, with exit 2, any other command holding the head of a lifted rule and the same command again.
When the command finishes the hook writes 201 and asks for the restore, which writes 204; else the sweep pane restores it once its 201 landed or its ttl passed.

procedure.title: Ask for and check a break glass
procedure.step: Ask: event.sh add --kind break.glass --code 300 --seat SEAT --ticket ID --action 'COMMAND' --note 'why the role cannot'. Then stop and wait; never run it or edit settings.
While one is active, 'seat.sh --check SEAT' exits 1 with one line naming it and its expiry; once over and verified it prints nothing and exits 0.
'seat.sh --audit' shows no kept-bypass line; the board's floor shows a row per request; the log holds its 300, 200, 100, 201 and 204, or its 423 and the reason.
A 423 'no owner answer': put the card on the page and ask the owner. 'already used': a second action needs a new 300 and a new answer.
Past its ttl in --check: run the restore verb with --why manual, then bring the sweep pane back with bring-up. 'did not verify after the restore': down the seat and bring it up again.

procedure.title: Set up the factory board on a repo
procedure.step: Copy the board tool into the repo, or point it at the tree with LOOP_ROOT and LOOP_CONFIG; the tool reads nothing outside the config's paths.
Edit the board config: out_dir (gitignored), poll and watch seconds (5 to 30 each, sum at most 30), inputs, line statuses, stations, kickback lanes naming routes rows, the build board.
Look before you serve: 'loop.sh collect --out FILE' derives and validates the entry, 'loop.sh render --in FILE --out DIR' draws it; open the page as a file.
Keep it current: 'loop.sh watch' in a labelled pane collects every watch_seconds and rewrites out_dir only when the floor changed; a failed pass keeps the last good page.
Serve it: point the page server's board_dir at out_dir and restart the tier; the board lint fails when they differ. GET /board is the page, /board/data.json its data, 503 if never built.
Prove it: the board suite, browser test and lint, then by eye: pr.opened shows the work at the tester, a hand-made PR shows opened by hand, a new record redraws the page within 30 s.

procedure.title: Run the blueprint view and its tiers
procedure.step: 'make -C report/loop render-blueprint' collects and renders into the dev tier; 'serve-dev' serves it and refreshes it every watch_seconds.
'promote-uat' gives uat the dev tier's current build and 'promote-stable' gives stable the uat build; a hand copy between tiers is never allowed.
Each tier's server runs in its reserved monitors slot (3.3.1 to 3.3.3); bring-up plugs them in, recovery restarts a killed one, and 'serve.sh --check TIER' probes a live but silent one.
Another repo, by config only: copy the board and blueprint tools, set the graph and work-order inputs, the links, the title and the key in the view config.
A new tier is a tier config that validates and names the tier it promotes from, a Make target pair, and one reserved monitors slot with a command and a check.
A ticket builds a component when the component id is in its title, Problem or Scope; an id in Notes, a criterion or the Outcome is a reference and does not count.

procedure.title: Build, check and send a briefing
procedure.step: Copy the page tool whole; only its three configs are repo-specific: the page config, the briefing rules and build inputs, and the briefing template.
Build: 'make -C tools/bearings sitrep-build TIER=T OUT=FILE'. Exit 3 means the payload breaks the standard and nothing is written; exit 4 means a source could not be read.
Check: 'make -C tools/bearings sitrep-check PAYLOAD=FILE'. Exit 0 may be sent; exit 1 prints one VIOLATION line per broken rule.
Send: 'make -C tools/bearings sitrep TIER=T PAYLOAD=FILE', with TO=message id when needed; the send runs the checker first and writes nothing when it fails.
Prove it: the tool's lint and suite from the labelled test pane: real and broken samples, a build from a synthetic repo, a live send and refusal, a browser seeing panel versus bubble.
On a refusal cut the clause that needs a subordinate clause to survive; never raise a limit. A wrong figure is fixed in the ticket or record it came from.

procedure.title: Adopt or resume a seat
procedure.step: Read the session id of the pane to adopt from the multiplexer's agent record for that pane.
Adopt from any shell in the same session: 'seat.sh --adopt --role R --pane P --session ID', with --ticket for a role whose label has a ticket. It types nothing into the pane.
Expect exit 3 for a pane with no claude agent, a contradicted session id, a taken name, or a second pane for a role that has its seat; a rerun with the same pane repairs.
The layout's other panes are not built; panes the role would have had stay where they are, and their wait loops are pointed at the adopted pane by hand.
The owner changes the session's model and permission mode in the pane when they want the role's; the rendered settings bind at the next start.
Restart from the conversation: end it, then run the seat script with --resume ID and --worktree set to the checkout the session ran in (door 2), or door 1 with --ticket.
Take an adopted seat back with 'seat.sh --down NAME': the old agent name and pane label return and seat.down 100 is recorded; no exit, no tab close, no slot return.

procedure.title: Give a seat its own test pane
procedure.step: Nothing by hand: the seat script builds 'test - herdr - SEAT' when the layout has a test slot, split under the monitor pane, exports COQ_TEST_PANE and names it in the brief.
The seat runs every make through 'testpane.sh $COQ_TEST_PANE CMD', which refuses any other pane with exit 3, so N seats hold N panes and no run queues.
The pane's shell stays in the checkout that brought the seat up, never in the slot, so a slot return on down cannot end it.
Check: 'seat.sh --check SEAT' exits 0 and the seat's tab holds three panes, agent, MONITOR and test; a lost one shows as 'pane missing: test - herdr - SEAT'.
A lost test pane: rerun the same seat command to split it back, then have the seat commit and push, down it and bring it up, since a running agent keeps its old COQ_TEST_PANE.
Down closes the seat's tab and its test pane; other seats' panes and the architect tab's test pane are untouched.
A layout with no test slot falls back to the architect tab's 'test - herdr' pane; a ticket seat on such a layout is refused before any lease when that tab has none.

procedure.title: Run the supervisor
procedure.step: Install once from the main checkout: 'make -C herdr supervisor-install' renders the service and timer, reloads and enables the timer; from a worktree slot it exits 3. Lingering must be on.
Each tick, 30 s after the last ends and 20 s after boot: halt flag, multiplexer, podman, bring-up, belt, owner page and wait loop, seats; a step is killed after 120 s, a tick after 420 s.
A reserved pane is healthy when its owner's label shows and a non-shell process is in front; a dead command is plugged in again; an open label under someone's job is left alone and reported.
A seat dead on two ticks 20 s apart is re-seated in its pane; it is skipped when younger than 90 s, under a fresh down lock, adopted or the monitor, and downed when its ticket is closed.
After 3 re-seats of one seat in 1800 s it stops and writes a 500: a runtime that dies every time is for a person.
When the owner page is down it serves it again joined to its session, then its wait loop; a page stopped on purpose is left alone, and the page key is never printed or logged.
Read it: 'make -C herdr supervisor-status', the unit's journal, slot 4.1.3, the supervisor's records; 'make -C herdr supervisor CHECK=1' runs a tick that changes nothing.
Stop it on purpose with the halt flag in the state dir, or 'make -C herdr supervisor-uninstall'. Retire any watcher armed by hand once the repo's watches run, or each record is announced twice.

A row whose do is ignore must not have to; every other row must have one.

section.code: Work taken or started: seat.up, seat.down, work.started, ticket.cut, pr.opened, note, and a break glass in effect. Housekeeping 100s are ignored by the table.
An integration or owner action finished: merged; break.glass granted by the owner; policy.applied, a standing default taken.
A gate passed: test.passed, review.passed, verified; and the one command of a break glass finished.
A break glass is over: the role settings are restored and verified.
A record moved on: request.forwarded, a break.glass request, the runner's record.routed receipt.
A request that fails the request schema, naming the failing key. No request schema exists in the source yet.
merge.conflict: the worker is woken with the PR, the head sha and the words merge main, and the merger is taken down.
In the locked set; no script or role emits it yet.
test.failed or review.changes, attempt 1 to 3, and the architect's rejected. Attempts 1 and 2 wake the worker; attempt 3 is escalated as 423.
blocked, escalated, a refused break glass, a stuck player. First to the architect, second to the owner as a decision; a policy may answer it after its deadline.
A seat refused over a cap, its role's max_seats or the host's max_agents; recorded as a 429 note and nothing is built.
The system failed: no route, a failed action or gate check, an unreadable or interrupted record, a failed node, a stall, a stalled or hand-started agent. Every 500 or more wakes the monitor.
section.family: Guard records use families GOV, CMP, RES, RCV and OPS: 1xx to 2xx normal, 3xx controller, 4xx pushback, 5xx recovery.
